newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends softer, further downtrend seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends softer, further downtrend seen.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly lower against its U.S. counterpart on Friday as many dealers said they expected a local depreciation trend for the medium term.
The local unit ended at T$27.549, off an intraday high of T$27.525, against Thursday's T$27.540 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$269 million.
Dealers noted active foreign fund inflows for the still bullish domestic stock market in afternoon trade, which helped push the local dollar toward its intraday high.
"U.S. dollar demand emerged again in late trade as many dealers believe the Taiwan dollar will tend to fall in the medium term because the pork export ban will hurt our exports," said one dealer.
"Some even forecast the local dollar will fall to T$28 by the end of this year," he said.
Taiwan on March 20 banned exports of fresh and frozen pork indefinitely due to an islandwide outbreak of the deadly contagious hog foot and mouth disease.

Experts say the pork export ban will reduce Taiwan's overall exports by 1.34 percent according to 1996 figures, cutting the island's trade surplus and, dealers say, pressuring the Taiwan dollar lower, dealers said.
Trading is suspended on Saturday for a national holiday.
For next week, a T$27.50-27.60 range was seen.
